Anna M: Heads-up — after yesterday's per-layer calibration tweak landed on canary, we see a regression on long-chat workloads. p95 latency +18%, throughput -22% for 8-token gen.
Mike R: Can you paste the before/after numbers? and which model/canary?
Anna M: Model: rdx-13b-quant-candidate. Canary group = 10% hosted traffic. Baseline (old calib): p50 42ms p95 87ms tput 520 req/s. New calib: p50 46ms p95 103ms tput 405 req/s.
Oliver K: Oof. Any flame/prof output? kernel selector logs?
Anna M: Yes — profiler snapshot and selector trace excerpt below. Looks like several mid layers are switching from 4-bit kernels back to fp16/FP8 fallback more often.
Anna M: ```
kernel_selector: chosen=quant_int4_opt kernel_latency=0.9ms
kernel_selector: chosen=fp8_fallback   kernel_latency=2.7ms reason=calib_mismatch layer=18
kernel_selector: chosen=fp8_fallback   kernel_latency=2.9ms reason=kv_layout_incompat layer=19
batcher: batch_size=1 dispatch=hot_path
KVCache: hit_rate=0.94 evictions=12/1000 seq_len=512
```
Sophia L: That `calib_mismatch` string rings bell — we changed per-layer zero-point heuristics to be stricter so some layers fail quant-compatibility checks and we force fallback. Could explain latency jump.
Mike R: Do we have a list of the sensitive layers causing fallbacks? maybe embeddings/lm_head excluded?
Anna M: Embedding & lm_head are excluded already. The noisy ones are around layers 16-21 (attention output and early MLP). I ran an A/B where I manually forced those layers to keep quant kernels (despite calib warnings) and latency recovered, but eval quality dropped ~0.6 BLEU-ish-equivalent metric on our probing prompts.
Oliver K: So tradeoff: keep quant kernels -> perf wins, small quality hit. Force fallbacks -> stable quality, perf regress. We need a middle ground: per-layer selective recalibration or softer threshold.
devops-bot: deploy-canary: rollback triggered for canary=rdx-13b-quant-candidate at 2026-05-02T14:12Z (reason: perf alert)
ci-bot: canary-pipeline: previous pipeline (revision abc123) passed tests at 14:03. New pipeline (revision def456) failed perf gate.
Sophia L: Another wrinkle — batching heuristics. The selector now tries to colocate requests for quant kernels to maximize throughput, but with our prefix caching pattern (many short chats) batcher often emits small batches; kernel dispatch overhead dominates for the fallback kernels (fp8/fp16), making p95 worse.
Mike R: Can you repro locally with controlled batch sizes? maybe we adjust dynamic batching thresholds for mixed-precision kernels.
Anna M: Repro script: ```python
# repro script snippet
for bs in [1,2,4,8]:
  run_bench(model='rdx-13b', quant='mixed', batch_size=bs, seq=64)
```
Results: bs=1 p95=108ms, bs=4 p95=94ms, bs=8 p95=82ms (new calib). Baseline bs=4 was 78ms. So batching helps but can't fully close gap.
Oliver K: Also saw KV cache churn higher when fallback kernels used — I think layout conversions between quant and fp kernels cause extra KV copy/transform costs. Logs show extra memcpy around kv-shards at layer boundary.
Anna M: Yep. Extract from trace: `kv_copy_time += 1.4ms per request` when layer set mismatched kernel formats.
Sophia L: Two-pronged approach suggested: (1) short term: revert strict calibration threshold + special-case layers 16-21 to keep quant kernels OR allow embedding/lm_head to be quant-tied if we can protect them. (2) longer: instrument per-layer sensitivity and run lightweight calibration on real traffic to build a tunable map.
Mike R: For (1) we can try lowering the mismatch penalty in kernel_selector for canaries and re-run perf gate. For (2) we should add a nightly job that samples inference traces and computes a per-layer quant-sensitivity score.
Oliver K: I can prototype a selector flag `--prefer-quant-soft` that biases toward quant kernels unless model loss delta > X on a mini-probe set. Quick patch and canary?
Anna M: Sounds good. Also let's add a temporary mitigation: if we detect mixed-format kv between consecutive layers, force an in-place layout conversion during warmup to amortize cost (avoid per-request memcpy).
devops-bot: perf-alert: p95_regression=+18% (rdx-13b-quant-candidate) triggered at 2026-05-02T14:10Z
Sophia L: Note on FP8 vs INT8: our FP8 kernels are faster on some hw (A100) but fallback behavior differs by length — FP8 runtime path currently has shorter vectorized kernels but is more sensitive to calibration skew. INT8 path is a bit more robust but slightly slower on small seqs. Worth trying INT8-only canary for the sensitive layers.
Mike R: Can you put a short checklist of experiments? I'll schedule time on the canary lane.
Anna M: Experiment list: 
- revert calibration threshold on canary (quick rollback)
- enable `--prefer-quant-soft` prototype and run perf gate
- try forcing INT8 for layers 16-21 and measure quality vs perf
- implement warmup in-place kv layout conversion (short PR)
- night job to compute per-layer sensitivity map (data collection + dashboard)

Anna M: I'll open PRs/Canary jobs and paste links. Thanks all — prioritizing the quick rollback + `prefer-quant-soft` so we don't impact hosted customers longer than necessary. :thumbsup:
Mike R: Thanks Anna — pls ping when canary shows green and we'll promote changes to dedicated lane.
Oliver K: I'll take the INT8 patch and a perf microbench for kv conversion.
Sophia L: I'll sketch the sensitivity pipeline and quick eval harness (small probe set).
ci-bot: job/rdx-13b/benchmark started (canary)
Anna M: Closing loop — opened issue #INF-724 with logs and repro. Will update thread with links.
